prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 中文 · 项目任务跟踪 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "编号" · longest unbreakable word 17px · one-line width 32px
  col 2: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "截止日期" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 87px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 598px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"说明 column is starved to ~3–4 characters per line, so every description becomes a tall vertical ribbon and rows balloon with dead space beside the short left cells; the date also splits as '2024-' / '03-15'. Width spent on 编号/负责人/状态 buys nothing since those were already one line, while the only column that needs space gets least."},"B":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"说明 gets a workable ~5–6 characters per line and 编号 stays intact, but 截止日期 fractures into three stacked fragments ('2024-' / '03-' / '15'), which destroys date comparability, and the 负责人 header wraps awkwardly while its data does not."},"C":{"grade":"poor","why":"The description column finally reads well (~12–13 chars/line) and the table is shortest, but the price is unacceptable: 编号 breaks as 'F-' / '12', names stack vertically, 状态 becomes '进/行/中' over three lines, and the 截止日期 header itself splits. Identifiers and statuses are the scan keys of a task tracker and they are shredded."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"Best balance: 编号, 负责人 data and 状态 all hold one line, dates break cleanly at a single hyphen ('2024-' / '03-15') so they stay readable as dates, and 说明 gets enough width (~6 chars/line) to read as prose rather than a ribbon. Header wraps are minor and row rhythm is consistent."},"E":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Dates stay whole on one line, which is genuinely valuable, and 编号/状态 are intact; but paying for that by crushing 说明 to ~3 characters per line makes the tallest table with the most wasted vertical space, and the description is the payload of this table."}},"best":["D"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Pixel widths are hard to read exactly from the renders, so my A-vs-D and B-vs-D description-width comparisons are eyeballed; also debatable whether a clean two-line date break (D) beats a whole one-line date (E) under stricter publication conventions."}
